subtopics.name: Care of clients with sensory impairment

questions.stem: A client who used fentanyl 6 hours ago is given a first dose of sublingual buprenorphine 8 mg to start treatment for opioid use disorder. Within 30 minutes the client has severe cramps, vomiting, sweating, gooseflesh, a runny nose, dilated pupils and restlessness. Heart rate is 118/min. Complete the diagram by placing the condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor.

actions.text: Notify the provider about giving more buprenorphine
Give naloxone to reverse the buprenorphine
Stop all treatment and discharge the client
Give a dose of fentanyl to stop the symptoms

parameters.text: Withdrawal score on the COWS scale
Body weight measured once a week
Bowel sounds in each of the four quadrants
Pupil response in both eyes each hour

rationale.correct: Buprenorphine is started when the client is already in moderate withdrawal (for example COWS 8 to 12 or more); starting too soon after full agonists precipitates withdrawal.

perOption.c1: Buprenorphine displaces full agonists such as fentanyl; giving it too soon after use causes sudden, severe withdrawal.
perOption.c2: Overdose causes pinpoint pupils and slow breathing, not this picture.
perOption.c3: Allergy causes hives and swelling, not withdrawal signs.
perOption.c4: The timing right after buprenorphine points to precipitated withdrawal.
perOption.a1: Additional buprenorphine often controls precipitated withdrawal.
perOption.a4: The client needs support and continued treatment.
perOption.a5: This is unsafe and not appropriate.
perOption.p2: Vomiting and sweating cause fluid loss.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client taking phenelzine, an MAOI, ate aged cheese and salami at a party. One hour later the client has a sudden, severe pounding headache, a stiff neck, palpitations and sweating. Blood pressure is 224/122 mm Hg. Complete the diagram by placing the condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor.

condition.text: Hypertensive crisis from a tyramine interaction

actions.text: Notify the provider and prepare an IV antihypertensive
Sit the client up and hold the MAOI as directed
Give an over-the-counter decongestant for the headache
Lay the client flat in bed with the legs raised on pillows
Wait for the headache to go away on its own with rest

parameters.text: Body weight measured once a week

rationale.correct: MAOI-tyramine hypertensive crisis: severe headache, stiff neck and hypertension; treat with rapid-acting antihypertensives and stop the MAOI.

perOption.c1: Tyramine-rich foods with an MAOI cause a sudden release of norepinephrine and severe hypertension.
perOption.c2: Serotonin syndrome causes clonus, fever and agitation after serotonergic drugs.
perOption.c3: Migraine does not raise blood pressure this high.
perOption.c4: Neck stiffness occurs, but the timing and blood pressure point to tyramine crisis.
perOption.a1: Rapid, controlled lowering of blood pressure prevents stroke.
perOption.a2: Upright positioning and removing the trigger help.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: After a 150 mg IV loading dose, a 70-year-old client in new atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular rate is to receive an amiodarone maintenance infusion at 1 mg/min. The pharmacy supplies amiodarone 450 mg in 250 mL of 5% dextrose in water. At what rate should the nurse set the pump? Round to one decimal place.

rationale.correct: 1 mg/min x 60 = 60 mg/hr. Concentration: 450 mg / 250 mL = 1.8 mg/mL. Rate: 60 / 1.8 = 33.33, which rounds to 33.3 mL/hr.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: A client with type 1 diabetes who often skips lunch is reviewing insulin action with the diabetes educator, assuming each insulin is given at 0800. For each insulin, indicate when the client is most at risk of hypoglycemia.

rationale.correct: Hypoglycemia risk follows insulin peaks: rapid-acting 1 to 2 hours, regular 2 to 4 hours, NPH 4 to 12 hours; long-acting basal insulins have little peak.

perOption.r1:c1: Rapid-acting insulin peaks about 1 to 2 hours after injection.
perOption.r2:c2: Regular insulin peaks about 2 to 4 hours after injection.
perOption.r3:c3: NPH peaks about 4 to 12 hours after injection.
perOption.r4:c4: Glargine has a relatively flat effect.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
American Diabetes Association Standards of Care
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Relate insulin peaks to hypoglycemia risk.

questions.stem: A client starting warfarin asks what to know about food and other drugs. Which instructions should the nurse give? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the amount of green leafy vegetables about the same each week
Avoid ibuprofen and aspirin unless the provider approves them
Tell every provider and pharmacist that you take warfarin
Stop eating all green vegetables while on warfarin
Get INR blood tests as scheduled
Take an extra dose if you miss one the day before

rationale.correct: Warfarin teaching: consistent vitamin K, avoid NSAIDs, report bleeding, tell all providers and keep INR appointments; do not double doses.

perOption.a: Consistent vitamin K intake keeps the INR stable.
perOption.d: Avoidance is not needed; consistency is the goal.
perOption.e: Dosing is guided by the INR.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Teach warfarin food and drug interactions.

questions.stem: The nurse is giving three crushable medications through a client's gastrostomy tube. Place the steps in order.

items.text: Flush the tube with 15 to 30 mL of water
Check tube placement and residual as policy directs
Give each medication separately, flushing with water between them
Flush with 15 to 30 mL of water after the last medication

rationale.correct: Medications by feeding tube: confirm placement, flush, give each drug separately with flushes between and flush at the end.

perOption.a: Confirm the tube is in the stomach.
perOption.d: Clears the tube and delivers the full dose.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: A client has received IV gentamicin and IV furosemide for 6 days. The client now reports ringing in the ears and feeling off balance when walking. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Tell the client this is expected and will stop when the infusion ends
Report the symptoms, since both drugs can damage hearing and balance
Give the next gentamicin dose faster so it finishes sooner
Ask the client to rest in bed until the ringing goes away

rationale.correct: Aminoglycosides cause ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity, and loop diuretics add to the ear risk; report tinnitus, hearing loss and dizziness.

perOption.b: Aminoglycosides and loop diuretics together increase the risk of ototoxicity.
perOption.c: Faster infusion increases peak levels and toxicity.
perOption.d: This does not address the drug toxicity.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client starting valproic acid for seizures asks why blood tests are needed. Which laboratory tests should the nurse explain will be monitored?

options.text: Thyroid tests, because valproate lowers thyroid hormone
Liver function tests and platelet counts over time
Potassium and magnesium, because valproate causes losses
Hemoglobin A1C, because valproate raises glucose

rationale.correct: Valproate monitoring includes liver function, platelets and drug levels; teach signs of liver injury and pancreatitis.

perOption.a: Thyroid effects are not the main concern.
perOption.b: Valproate can cause liver injury and low platelets.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each inhaled device, choose the key technique to teach.

options.text: Shake it, then breathe in slowly and deeply and hold the breath
Breathe in as hard and fast as possible
Do not shake the canister
Breathe in quickly and forcefully, and do not breathe out into the device
Shake it well before each use
Breathe in slowly over 5 seconds
Breathe normally through the mouthpiece until the mist stops
Take one deep breath and stop
Hold the breath for 30 seconds after each breath

rationale.correct: MDI: shake, slow deep breath and hold. Dry powder: fast forceful breath, no shaking. Nebulizer: normal breathing until the mist stops.

perOption.b1:a: Slow inhalation carries the spray into the lungs.
perOption.b1:b: Fast breathing is for dry powder inhalers.
perOption.b2:a: A fast, deep breath draws the powder in; moisture clumps the powder.
perOption.b2:b: Dry powder inhalers are not shaken.
perOption.b2:c: Slow breathing does not lift the powder.
perOption.b3:a: Normal breathing delivers the drug over several minutes.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: A client is scheduled to receive cisplatin chemotherapy. Which nursing action best prevents a major toxicity of this drug?

options.text: Restrict fluids for 12 hours before the infusion to reduce nausea
Give IV fluids before and after and monitor kidney function
Keep the client in a dark room to prevent any light sensitivity
Give the drug quickly over 5 minutes to shorten the exposure

rationale.correct: Cisplatin causes nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity and severe nausea; prevent with hydration, electrolyte replacement and antiemetics.

perOption.b: Hydration protects the kidneys from cisplatin nephrotoxicity.
perOption.c: Light sensitivity is not the main concern.
perOption.d: Rapid infusion does not prevent toxicity.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client is to start parenteral nutrition with a lipid emulsion. Which history should the nurse report to the provider before starting the lipids?

options.text: A history of lactose intolerance
A severe allergy to eggs or soy
A history of seasonal allergies to pollen
A recent sore throat

rationale.correct: Check for egg and soy allergy before lipid emulsions; watch for fever, chills and back pain during the first infusion.

perOption.b: Many lipid emulsions contain egg phospholipids and soybean oil.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: Before the 0900 medications, the nurse reviews new data. Highlight the findings that are reasons to hold a scheduled medication and call the provider.

segments.text: is NPO for a CT with IV contrast at 1100
has new unexplained muscle pain and dark urine

rationale.correct: Hold and report medications when levels or findings suggest toxicity or risk, such as a high lithium level, contrast with metformin or statin muscle injury.

perOption.s2: Above the usual range; lithium should be held and reported.
perOption.s4: Metformin is often held around contrast in clients at risk.
perOption.s8: This suggests rhabdomyolysis; hold and report.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Laboratory reference ranges as used in common NCLEX review texts; follow the facility's ranges

questions.stem: A 45-year-old client with rheumatoid arthritis who grew up in a country where tuberculosis is common is about to start adalimumab, a tumor necrosis factor inhibitor. Which test should be done before the first dose?

options.text: A hemoglobin A1C to check for diabetes
A screening test for latent tuberculosis
A bone density scan to check for osteoporosis
A lipid panel to check cholesterol

rationale.correct: Before biologics such as TNF inhibitors, screen for latent TB and hepatitis B; teach infection precautions and avoid live vaccines.

perOption.b: TNF inhibitors can reactivate latent TB, so screening is needed first.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Screen before starting a TNF inhibitor.

questions.stem: A resident with advanced dementia becomes frightened and strikes out during showers. Which approach to hygiene is most appropriate?

options.text: Have two staff members hold the resident so the shower can be finished quickly
Use a calm approach and a towel bath in bed, explaining each step
Skip bathing until the resident asks for a shower
Give a sedative before each shower so the resident stays calm

rationale.correct: For clients with dementia who resist bathing, use calm, person-centered methods such as towel baths and adjust the timing.

perOption.a: Restraining increases fear and the risk of injury.
perOption.b: Person-centered bathing, such as a towel bath, reduces distress.
perOption.c: Hygiene still needs to be met.
perOption.d: Routine sedation is not the first choice.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Provide hygiene to a resident with dementia.

questions.stem: A nurse on a medical unit reviews the stool descriptions charted by assistive personnel for four clients. For each stool finding, indicate the most likely cause.

rows.text: Bright red blood on the surface of the stool

columns.text: Upper GI bleeding or iron supplements
A narrowing or obstruction in the colon

rationale.correct: Stool clues: black and tarry (upper bleeding or iron), clay-colored (biliary obstruction), bright red (lower bleeding) and ribbon-like (colon narrowing).

perOption.r1:c1: Digested blood or iron makes stool black.
perOption.r2:c2: Lack of bile makes stool pale.
perOption.r3:c3: Bright red blood comes from the lower GI tract.
perOption.r4:c4: Narrow stool suggests a narrowing in the colon.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client receiving chemotherapy has nausea despite prescribed antiemetics. Which nondrug measures should the nurse suggest? Select all that apply.

options.text: Eat small, frequent meals
Avoid strong food smells and greasy foods
Try ginger or acupressure wristbands
Lie flat right after eating
Drink large amounts of fluid with each meal
Use relaxation or distraction

rationale.correct: Nondrug measures for nausea: small meals, avoiding odors and fatty foods, ginger, acupressure, relaxation and staying upright after eating.

perOption.a: Small meals are easier to tolerate.
perOption.b: Odors and fat can trigger nausea.
perOption.e: Large volumes with meals can worsen nausea.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client with a right-sided stroke ignores the left side of the body and eats only from the right side of the tray. Which nursing approach is most appropriate?

options.text: Place everything on the client's right side so the client can reach it
Teach the client to scan to the left, with reminders
Keep the left side covered with a blanket so the client is not upset by it
Feed the client to save time

rationale.correct: For unilateral neglect, teach scanning toward the affected side, use cues and protect the affected side from injury.

perOption.a: This avoids the neglect but does not help the client learn to compensate.
perOption.b: Scanning training helps clients with left-sided neglect attend to the neglected side.
perOption.d: This reduces independence and does not address neglect.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

rationale.correct: Low Braden subscale scores show which risks to target, such as sensory loss, moisture and limited mobility.

perOption.r6: Some risk, but not the lowest score.

questions.stem: The nurse teaches a client with insomnia progressive muscle relaxation. Which statement shows the client understands the technique?

options.text: "I'll tense, then relax each muscle group in turn, feet first."
"I'll keep my muscles tight until I feel tired enough to fall asleep."
"I'll do vigorous exercise right before bed so I relax afterward."
"I'll lie still and try hard to force myself to fall asleep."

rationale.correct: Progressive muscle relaxation involves tensing and then releasing muscle groups in sequence to reduce tension before sleep.

perOption.a: Tensing and releasing muscle groups in sequence is progressive muscle relaxation.
perOption.c: Vigorous exercise at bedtime can make sleep harder.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client on intake and output monitoring received 1,250 mL of IV fluid, drank two 240 mL glasses of juice and one 160 mL cup of broth, and had 480 mL of tube feeding plus 120 mL of water flushes over 24 hours. The client also had 2 ice-chip cups that the unit counts as half their volume, each cup holding 200 mL. What is the client's total intake for 24 hours in milliliters?

rationale.correct: IV 1,250 + juice 480 + broth 160 + tube feeding 480 + flushes 120 + ice chips (2 x 100) 200 = 2,690 mL.
references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)

questions.stem: A client is being fitted for axillary crutches. Which finding shows the crutches are the correct height?

options.text: The crutch pads touch the armpits when the client stands
A gap of 2 to 3 finger widths between armpit and pad
The elbows are straight when holding the hand grips
The crutch tips are placed right next to the client's toes

rationale.correct: Correct crutch fit: 2 to 3 finger widths below the armpit, elbows bent about 30 degrees and tips about 15 cm to the side and front.

perOption.a: Pressure in the armpits can damage nerves.
perOption.b: This gap prevents pressure on the nerves in the armpit.
perOption.c: The elbows should bend about 30 degrees.
perOption.d: Tips are placed about 15 cm (6 in) to the side and front of the feet.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The family of a dying client is frightened because the client's breathing has periods of deep, fast breaths followed by pauses of up to 30 seconds. What should the nurse explain?

options.text: "This means the client is choking and needs suctioning right away."
"This pattern is common near death and rarely distressing."
"This means the client needs to go back to the hospital for a ventilator."
"This pattern means the client is in severe pain right now."

rationale.correct: Cheyne-Stokes respirations are common near death; explain them to the family and focus on comfort.

perOption.a: This is a breathing pattern, not choking.
perOption.b: Cheyne-Stokes breathing is common at the end of life; the nurse explains and supports the family.
perOption.c: This is not consistent with comfort-focused care.
perOption.d: It is not a sign of pain by itself.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse is inserting an indwelling urinary catheter. Place the steps in order.

items.text: Perform hand hygiene and explain the procedure
Open the sterile kit and put on sterile gloves
Inflate the balloon and secure the catheter to the leg
Insert the catheter until urine flows, then advance slightly
Clean the urinary meatus with antiseptic

rationale.correct: Catheter insertion: prepare, open the sterile kit with sterile gloves, clean the meatus, insert until urine flows, inflate the balloon and secure.

perOption.c: Reduces bacteria at the entry site.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Insert a urinary catheter in order.

questions.stem: A client on suicide precautions asks for a razor to shave before visitors arrive. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Give the razor and check on the client in 15 minutes
Offer an electric razor or supervise shaving per policy
Tell the client shaving is not allowed while on the unit
Ask the visitors to bring a disposable razor from home

rationale.correct: On suicide precautions, remove means of harm and meet grooming needs with supervision or safer alternatives.

perOption.a: A razor is a means of self-harm.
perOption.b: Supervised or safer alternatives meet the need while keeping the client safe.
perOption.c: Basic grooming should be supported safely.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Meet grooming needs safely on suicide precautions.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old client who recently lost their sight from diabetic retinopathy refuses to leave the room and asks staff to do everything for them. Which approach best supports adjustment?

options.text: Do the client's care for them until they feel ready to try
Acknowledge the loss and refer to low-vision rehabilitation
Tell the client that many people live well without sight and they should try harder
Leave the client alone so they can grieve in private

rationale.correct: Support adjustment to disability by acknowledging the loss, referring to rehabilitation and encouraging gradual independence.

perOption.b: Validating feelings and building skills support adjustment to sudden vision loss.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
